problems.title: Heine-Cantor theorem
problems.objective: Upgrade continuity on a compact set to uniform continuity.
problems.statement: Prove a continuous function on a compact metric space is uniformly continuous.
permittedResults: Continuity gives a local radius at each point.
problems.strategy: First: For each $x$, choose a neighborhood where function values stay within $\varepsilon/2$ of $f(x)$. Next: Extract finitely many half-radius balls covering the compact domain. Finally: Use the minimum selected half-radius and a shared center to compare nearby points.
hints: For each $x$, choose a neighborhood where function values stay within $\varepsilon/2$ of $f(x)$.
Extract finitely many half-radius balls covering the compact domain.
Use the minimum selected half-radius and a shared center to compare nearby points.
problems.solution: If the domain is empty, uniform continuity is vacuous. Otherwise fix $\varepsilon>0$. For each $x$ choose $r_x>0$ such that $d(x,u)<r_x$ implies $d(f(x),f(u))<\varepsilon/2$. Compactness supplies a nonempty finite cover by half-radius balls $B_{r_{x_i}/2}(x_i)$. Set $\delta=\min_i(r_{x_i}/2)>0$. If $d(y,z)<\delta$, choose $i$ with $d(y,x_i)<r_{x_i}/2$. Then $d(z,x_i)\le d(z,y)+d(y,x_i)<\delta+r_{x_i}/2\le r_{x_i}$. Both $f(y)$ and $f(z)$ are within $\varepsilon/2$ of $f(x_i)$, so the triangle inequality gives $d(f(y),f(z))<\varepsilon$. The number $\delta$ depends only on $\varepsilon$, proving uniform continuity.

problems.objective: Prove an interval cannot be separated into two relatively open pieces.

If $s\in U$, relative openness gives points of $U$ just to the right of $s$, contradicting its upper-bound property (unless $s=b$, impossible since $b\in V$).
